svg.text: 5069-IB16 · 24 V DC sinking module, sourcing field devices · every field input lands on a terminal, never directly on the module
WHY IT IS WIRED THIS WAY
Every input lands on a terminal.
No field wire goes directly onto the module. The module can
then be replaced without disturbing field wiring, and every
signal can be tested and disconnected at a terminal.
Drive healthy, thermistor, seal water, stop. A broken wire
opens the circuit and reads as a FAULT, not as healthy.
Fail-safe by wiring, not by programming.
Local AND Remote as separate inputs. One input can only tell
you two things and cannot tell you it is broken. Two inputs
distinguish Local, Remote, Off — and detect a selector
Grouped at the end of the block, not scattered. A contiguous
block of spares is usable; scattered spares are not.
Separate from the analogue loop group (ECP4) so a field
digital short cannot take every instrument reading down at
Signals grouped by EQUIPMENT, not by module convenience
1. 5069-IB16 is a sinking input module fed by sourcing field devices. Field power for this group comes from ECP2 (SCH-0030).
2. NO FIELD WIRE LANDS DIRECTLY ON A PLC MODULE. Every input passes through a terminal on rail X3.
3. Critical inputs are wired NORMALLY CLOSED so a broken wire reads as a fault rather than as healthy. Verified at FAT by test K-83:
disconnect the field wire and confirm the signal reads FAULT.
4. Volt-free contacts are used from the field wherever possible. Where a field device provides a voltage output, an interposing relay is used.
5. Spare points are terminated, labelled and grouped at the end of the equipment block. FAT test K-82 verifies they are available.
6. This sheet is the contract between the electrical package and the systems integrator. It must be issued on a transmittal at the SAME
revision as the board — FAT defect FD-004 was caused by the integrator working from an earlier I/O list revision.
RAW WATER TRANSFER PUMP STATION — MCC-01
